Instead, I'm looking at my DSA notes and this corporate contract, feeling like I sold my soul for a cubicle. Why does achieving my dream feel like a death sentence?

But I'm sitting in this web dev lab and it's just mind-numbing. Everyone around me is building these insane projects and talking about open-source contributions, and I'm just staring at a broken React component wanting to cry. I fought so hard for this seat, but now that I'm here, I realize I don't even like it. I feel like an absolute fraud.

I study, I memorize the slides, I regurgitate them in the exam, and I get the grade. But if you ask me what I actually learned or what I want to do with my life, my mind is a complete blank. I'm terrified that I'm just a perfect student on paper who has absolutely no real soul or purpose inside.

I worked all summer for this prestigious research internship because I thought it would make me feel like a 'real scientist'. Well, I'm here now, and it's just Excel sheets, formatting citations, and cleaning glass tubes while the grad students ignore me. Is this the 'glamorous' academic life I burned myself out for during the semesters? I look at my senior professors who look so exhausted and miserable, and I just feel this cold dread. If this is the peak, why am I even trying?

Everyone said college would be the best four years of my life. I expected late-night deep conversations, a close-knit group of friends who 'get' me, and finding my true passion. Instead, I'm a sophomore, and my days are just running from lectures to the mess hall, sitting alone in the library, and pretending to be busy on my phone when I see people walking together. The reality of this place is so incredibly mundane and lonely compared to what I built up in my head. I feel like I'm failing at the 'college experience'.

I did everything right. I ground for months, pulled all-nighters for coding tests, got a 9.6 CGPA, and finally landed the 'dream' FAANG internship everyone was killing for. I sat at my desk on Monday, looked at the codebase, and felt this terrifying wave of emptiness. Is this it? Is this the prize? I went to the washroom and cried because I realized I absolutely hate this, but I've spent my entire college life building up to this exact moment. I feel so scammed by my own ambitions.

Since school, my parents said 'just clear JEE and get into a tier-1 college, then your life is set.' Now I'm in my third year of CSE, struggling to survive DSA coding labs, and realizing the 'set life' is just an endless, soul-crushing loop of sprint retrospectives, corporate buzzwords, and chasing packages to show off to relatives. The expectation of peace at the end of this tunnel was a lie. I'm running on fumes for a future I don't even want anymore.

Instead, I stared at the marksheet PDF and felt absolutely nothing—just a heavy, dead numbness. I fought so hard, cried so many nights over failing, and now that I passed, I'm just back at zero with no idea who I am or why I even cared. The relief I built up in my head doesn't exist.

I managed to get a decent core job offer, but the gap between the shiny external validation and the sheer anxiety I feel inside is making me sick. I expected landing a job to cure my insecurity, but it has only made me feel like an imposter who took a path that belongs to someone else.

Now I'm buried in rote thermodynamics formulas, bureaucratic defense-sector presentation slides, and absolute boredom. The expectations I had of this branch being a poetic, scientific pursuit are completely dead, and now I'm just another roll number memorizing derivations for a GPA that means nothing to me.

I thought getting that '9+' tag and seeing my name highlighted on the placement cell shortlist would make me feel like I finally arrived, like I was finally safe. Instead, I'm sitting here in the dark, wondering why I killed myself working 14 hours a day for this hollow emptiness. If achieving the dream feels this dead, what the hell am I even running for?

After months of sacrificing my sleep, skipping hanging out with friends, and literally crying over my DSA sheets, I finally saw my name in the top 5% on the grade sheet today—a perfect 9.4 GPA. I thought I would feel this massive rush of relief, like a weight lifting off my chest. Instead, I just looked at the PDF, shut my laptop, and went to bed feeling this terrifyingly hollow emptiness. Everyone is texting me congratulations, but I feel like an absolute fraud who ran a marathon only to find out there's nothing at the finish line.

I fought so hard to transition into CS because of the campus placement stats and the pressure from everyone saying it’s the only path to a stable life. Now I’m sitting in these daily operating systems and compiler design lectures, looking at the slides, and feeling my chest tighten up with pure dread. I convinced myself that once I got the branch change, the passion would just show up. It didn’t, and now I'm stuck in a multi-year commitment for a future I don't even want, feeling completely alienated from the person I used to be.

Everyone on my LinkedIn feed is posting those generic 'I am thrilled to announce my summer internship at...' updates, and I posted mine too because of the social pressure. But the reality of my daily corporate routine is soul-crushing; I spend nine hours a day fixing minor bugs on a legacy codebase that nobody cares about. I expected this milestone to make me feel secure and grown-up, but it's only made me realize how terrifyingly empty the corporate ladder actually is. I'm dreading graduation because I feel like I'm marching straight into a trap I built with my own hands.

I did everything the college roadmaps told me to do—solved hundreds of LeetCode problems, built three full-stack projects, and spent my entire semester break grinding. Yesterday, during a peer gathering, everyone was talking about system design and frameworks, and I suddenly felt this overwhelming wave of disgust and exhaustion. I realized I don't care about any of this; I only did it to survive the placement rat race. I've spent three years building a version of myself that everyone else approves of, but I look in the mirror and have absolutely no clue who is looking back at me.

Everyone said once you clear JEE and get into CS, life is set. I worked my ass off, scored 9.4 CGPA, got the DSA lab credits, and secured a 15 LPA summer internship today. But I literally went back to my hostel room, locked the door, and stared at the ceiling. I felt absolutely nothing. No joy, no relief. Just this terrifying emptiness. If this is what winning feels like, why does it feel like a dead end?

My parents kept comparing me to my cousin who got placed in London. I finally cracked a decent product role, not London but still good, right? I thought they'd be proud, thought I'd finally feel like I belong at the dinner table. Instead, my dad just asked if I can try for a double-switch next year to match his package. I feel like an absolute fraud. No matter how much I grind or how many coding contests I win, the goalpost just moves further away. I'm so tired.

I took up Mechanical because I genuinely loved building things as a kid. Now I'm in my third year, drowning in mindless CAD assignments, thermal engineering derivations, and zero actual creativity. It's just rote memorization to pass the midterms. I thought college would be this grand space of innovation and intellect, but it feels like a factory floor producing paper degrees. I don't even know why I get up at 8 AM anymore.

Everyone on LinkedIn is posting about their summer research fellowships and machine learning internships. I got one too, at a pretty decent lab. I expected to feel like I was finally 'making it'. But when I sit down to code, I just feel this massive imposter syndrome. I don't care about neural networks, I'm just doing it because it's the 'it' thing. I'm living a life scripted by algorithms and peer pressure, and the real me is completely missing from the picture.

I thought getting into my dream college would solve everything. Back in school, I was the topper, the smart kid who had it all figured out. Now, I'm just average here, struggling to keep my CGPA above 7.5, failing coding rounds in the first screening itself. The mismatch between who I thought I'd be at twenty and this anxious, struggling person staring back in the mirror is killing me. I don't even recognize myself anymore.

I just got my 4th sem results back and I hit a 9.4 CGPA. My parents are literally boasting on the family WhatsApp group about my DSA lab scores and how I'm 'on track' for a massive day-one placement. But honestly? I stared at that PDF marksheet for an hour and just felt this cold, dead numbness. I did everything right, slept 4 hours a night, memorized leetcode patterns, and now that I have the numbers, I feel absolutely nothing. If this 'success' feels this empty, what the hell am I even killing myself for?

Everyone in my batch is dying to get into this fintech firm, and I somehow cleared the technical rounds and got the internship offer. When the HR called, I had to fake this high-pitched excitement because my roommates were watching, but the second they left the room, I threw up in the washroom. I'm looking at the 12-hour workday, the corporate lingo, the soul-sucking desk, and realizing this is the 'dream' I sacrificed my hobbies and sleep for. I feel like a fraud who just won a prize she desperately doesn't want.

I fought with my parents for two years to let me take CSE instead of Civil because I thought writing code was where the magic happens and where I'd finally feel smart. Now I'm sitting in this compiler design lecture, surrounded by people who code in their sleep, looking at my dry, broken terminal screen, and I just feel this immense wave of regret. I forced my way into this 'elite' branch, and now that I'm here, I hate it, but I can't even tell my parents because they'll say 'we told you so'. I'm stuck in a trap I built with my own hands.

I spent my entire high school life locked in a room studying for entrance exams, telling myself that once I get into this tier-1 college, everything would be perfect and I'd find my 'people'. I've been here three months now. The campus is beautiful, yes, but the conversations are just endlessly about packages, off-campus referrals, and who got what rank in Codeforces. It's just high school competitive toxicity but on steroids. I worked so hard to get here, but I've never felt this lonely or disconnected in my entire life.

I signed my job offer letter yesterday. 14 LPA, fully remote, tech stack I actually know. It’s literally what my seniors said was the 'golden ticket' to a sorted life. But instead of celebrating, I slept for 14 hours and woke up feeling this terrifying sense of pointlessness. Is this it? For the next 40 years, I just write APIs, get sprint points, wait for weekends, and buy stuff to distract myself? I thought clearing placements would feel like crossing a finish line, but it feels like I just walked into a lifelong waiting room.

I finally got that 9.2 CGPA this semester, and my parents are literally boasting on WhatsApp about my upcoming summer internship at a FAANG company. But honestly? I felt absolutely nothing when the portal updated. I thought I'd feel like a king, but I just sat at my desk looking at the screen, feeling this heavy, hollow disappointment. I spent three years sacrificing sleep, skipping weekend outings, grinding LeetCode, just to feel like a ghost in my own life.

Everyone said 'work hard till 12th grade, get into a top tier engineering college, and your life is set.' Well, I'm here now, sitting through these endless, dry lectures on compiler design, looking at my classmates who only talk about CTC, packages, and referral links. This isn't learning; it's just a glorified, high-stress trade school. I expected to find passion and brilliant minds, but all I found is a factory line of code monkeys, and I feel so cheated.

I spent the last six months prepping day and night for the campus placements, thinking that getting a high-paying offer would finally stop the anxiety and make my family proud. I got the offer letter yesterday—30 LPA base—and my dad actually hugged me. But today, the anxiety is worse than ever because now I realize I have to actually show up and do this soul-crushing corporate job for the next forty years. The prize for winning the rat race is just being a faster rat.

I took CSE because the internet and my relatives made it sound like this magical world where you build cool stuff and change the world. Instead, I'm stuck in a stuffy lab debugging ancient Java code that I don't care about, just to clear a backlog. I thought college would be this grand awakening where I found my purpose, but I'm just tired, lonely, and realizing my actual days are incredibly mundane and utterly pointless.

I worked my ass off to get into this premium design program, thinking I'd finally be surrounded by creative soulmates who want to build beautiful things. Instead, it’s just a massive ego-fest of people trying to look trendy on LinkedIn and curating their 'aesthetic' portfolios for UI/UX internships. I expected collaborative art, but I got cutthroat commercialism, and I feel so isolated because nobody here actually cares about the craft.

I literally killed myself for two years to crack this 12 LPA internship. I skipped family events, ruined my sleep schedule, lived on Red Bull, and crammed DSA trees and graphs until my brain turned to mush. Now I’m sitting in this air-conditioned office, doing these brain-dead daily standups and updating Jira tickets, and I just... feel nothing. I thought landing this would make me feel like a god, but I just feel like a highly paid, exhausted cog in a machine that doesn't care if I live or die. Why did I sacrifice my entire youth for this?

Just got my 6th sem results back and I’m sitting on a 9.5 CGPA. My parents are bragging on the family WhatsApp group, telling everyone I'm set for life. But I’m staring at my marksheet in the dark and I feel like throwing up. I don't know anything about who I am outside of getting these stupid numbers on a PDF. I built this whole identity around being 'the smart kid,' and now that I have the grades, I feel completely hollow and directionless.

I fought so hard with my parents to take CS instead of Mechanical because everyone said CS is where the money and 'cool lifestyle' is. Now I'm sitting in this web dev lab, looking at React code, and I want to claw my eyes out. Everyone around me is talking about open-source contributions and system design like it’s oxygen, and I have to fake being excited just to fit in. I got what I wanted, but the reality is a nightmare and I'm trapped because my parents paid a massive donation fee for this seat.

I spent my entire high school life studying for JEE, telling myself 'just two years of grind and then college will be amazing.' I imagined finding my tribe, late-night tea sessions, and actually living. Cut to now: I'm in my second year of college, and my life is just going from my hostel room to the library to a DSA coding lab. The peer groups are so transactional, everyone only talks to you if they want your assignment files or referral codes. This is not what I signed up for.

I just got placed at a big consulting firm today. Everyone is congratulating me, my phone is blowing up with LinkedIn notifications, and my dad is literally crying tears of joy on the phone. But when I went to the washroom, I just stared at myself in the mirror and broke down crying because I feel this overwhelming dread. I don't want to build PowerPoint decks for eighty hours a week; I want to write music or do literally anything else. I feel like a fraud who just signed away the next five years of my life for corporate slavery.
